The Long Jump saw us gain the first two places through the agency of Clemens and Fleming, although Basford in winning the club Long Jump Handicap did so well that it was a pity he did not count in the match event.
At our evening meeting on May 20th, eight Club handicaps were held, and a noticeable feature was the double successes of three members, G. Basford, B.
Basford. Basford got in front of the King's College Hospital sprinter down the straight and stayed in the lead to win his first championship.

We have always looked upon ourselves as being rather weak in the sprinting line, but with men like Basford, Read, Jarvis, Wilcock, not forgetting our veteran Morrie Odell, we are likely to shew some improvement in this department.

Scrimshaw, Tosh, Clemens, Holder, Allum, Michael, Ford, Kench, Tame, Basford and Jarvis all performed creditably in the highest class without being able to claim one of the first four places which alone carry points to the Club's credit.
Basford. Jarvis made a good start for us and at the end of the third stage we were third,the Polytechnic H. leading.
Basford and F. Powter, and we managed to take third place.
Our team, Michael, Jarvis, Basford and Read, ran very well and together with the other men who have represented us so ably in these League events, deserve our very best thanks.

In the 4 x 100 yards we had to turn out two half-milers, in Kench and Frank Webb, our only two sprinters being Basford and Bone. Croydon won this event from Mitcham and incidentally this was Mitcham's only defeat of the evening.

Morgan was seen out in our team and ran well, but Wilson was rather a weak link and Basford had to give way to Pallett over the last stage. On June 17th the 1 Mile Team race was held at the Civil Service meeting, and here Herne Hill H. scored a surprise win and so consolidated their lead at the head of the table.
Basford led off well for us by capturing the sprint; and later Kench, our mile champion, surprised everyone by his excellent running in the 440 yards event, which he won in fast time.
In the fourth of the six events, held at the "Kinnaird" meeting, a relay 4 x 220 yards, were placed third, Stroud, Kealey, Pack and Basford forming our team.
